note: Read in the Laws of Guyana as the Ministry of Legal Affairs publishes them (mola.gov.gy, revised edition L.R.O. 1/2012). Majority: 18, the reading being the Infancy Act (Cap. 46:01), which holds an infant may not act as executor until 'the full age of eighteen years' (s. 6, O. 4/1974) and gives the court powers over a married infant's property until eighteen; marriage makes an infant of full age (s. 9): not held. No separate Age of Majority Act was in the ministry's index of chapters 1 to 2 and 45 to 46. Work: 15. Employment of Young Persons and Children Act (Cap. 99:01, as amended to Act 9 of 1999): a child is under fifteen, and no child shall be admitted to employment or work in any occupation (s. 3(1)); young persons (15 and over, under 16) may not work at night in industrial undertakings: not held. Performers: barred, the reading being that s. 3 admits no child to work 'in any occupation' and the Act has no exception for performers. Service: none. The Defence Act (Cap. 15:01) raises the regular Force by enlistment of a person offering to enlist, who must understand the notice and wish to be enlisted (s. 18).
